title: Why Form Leads Disappear After Submit
description: A fictional workflow demo showing how ownership, alerts, logs and retries give each incoming lead a visible next step.
hook: The form says submitted. So where did the lead go?

scenes.voiceover: The form says submitted. So where did the lead go?
scenes.subtitle: Where did the lead go?
scenes.visual_prompt: Original form card sends a glowing lead into a dark workflow; fictional UI recreation label visible

scenes.voiceover: A success message only proves that the browser sent something.
scenes.subtitle: Submitted is only the start.
scenes.visual_prompt: Split view: browser success check on left, unassigned workflow node on right; original diagram

scenes.voiceover: The server still needs to validate it, save it, and assign a clear owner.
scenes.subtitle: Validate. Save. Assign.
scenes.visual_prompt: Owned recording of a local demo showing validation, database write and owner field; hide secrets

scenes.voiceover: Then send an alert with one next step, and keep a log if delivery fails.
scenes.subtitle: Alert + next step + log
scenes.visual_prompt: Original three-node diagram connecting alert, action and error log; no third-party logos

scenes.voiceover: Use an idempotency key so a retry cannot create the same lead twice.
scenes.subtitle: Retry without duplicates.
scenes.visual_prompt: Owned local test: repeat the same request and show one stored record; blur local identifiers

scenes.voiceover: Now every lead has an owner, a history, and a visible way forward. Review the workflow before you ship it.
scenes.subtitle: Give every lead a way forward.
scenes.visual_prompt: Original friendly teal robot guides one golden star through a safe illuminated workflow exit; no text or logos

cta: Save this checklist and test one real form path before release.

source_notes.claim: This is a fictional workflow demonstration, not a measured client result.
source_notes.note: Replace screen recordings only with owned project footage.
